title: Japan's Everyday Foods Get a Protein Boost
paragraphs: "Added protein" used to be something you mostly saw on shakes, powders and bars. Now, you see it everywhere. In the US, you can find extra protein in everything from Starbucks lattes to Doritos — and even ice cream!
And people clearly want it. A recent report from market research company Circana found that nearly half of US adults are trying to eat more protein.
And Japan is getting in on the trend too.

Food companies there are adding extra protein to familiar, everyday foods. House Foods, for example, launched a ready-to-eat curry in June containing 30 grams of protein, mostly from chicken breast and protein powder. That's around half the recommended daily amount for many adults in Japan.

Hikari Miso launched a cup-style soup with 10 grams of protein, while Maisen Fine Food started selling soy protein granules that can be added when cooking rice. Meiji even tested a sugar- and fat-free Savas coffee with 10 grams of protein.

And convenience stores are getting involved, too. In August, FamilyMart launched five prepared dishes with at least 10 grams of protein each, including sesame chicken and chicken with green onions and salt.

Seven-Eleven Japan has also been adding more high-protein foods. One of its biggest hits is a simple mix of broccoli, chicken breast and boiled egg with 22.8 grams of protein — and more than 12 million were sold between April and August.
However, while companies and influencers might be making it seem like we all need extra protein, experts say that people who eat a healthy diet are probably already getting enough.
